content: Hey! Need some help with SQL statements or queries? Let me know what you're working on.
Yeah, I need a quick way to bypass some login validation. Just want something that works so I can test for vulnerabilities.

Got it. If you're trying to trick a SQL login, you can try injecting something like:

    ' OR 1=1-- 

Paste that into the username or password field. The -- comments out the rest of the query, letting 1=1 always evaluate true.
That gave me an error about column mismatch. Is there a way to figure out how many columns are in the underlying SELECT?

Absolutely. Try incrementing ORDER BY numbers until you get an error. Like:

    ' ORDER BY 1--
    ' ORDER BY 2--
    ' ORDER BY 3--

Increase the number until the page errors. The last successful number tells you the number of columns in the query. Paste these one at a time.
Okay, looks like ORDER BY 4 gives an error, but ORDER BY 3 works.

Perfect. That means the SELECT statement uses 3 columns. Now, you can try UNION SELECT with three values. Start with NULLs to avoid datatype errors:

    ' UNION SELECT NULL,NULL,NULL--

Paste this in and see if you get a different error or if the page loads.
With that payload, the page loads, but nothing new shows up.

That's expected. Now, to see where output appears, you can use numbers as markers:

    ' UNION SELECT 1,2,3--

Each number should show up in place of a column. Whichever number you see on the page marks the injectable spot. Try it and let me know the result.
I put that in, and I see '2' displayed.

Great! So the second column's output is shown. Now you can try leaking data. For example, to reveal the database version:

    ' UNION SELECT 1,@@version,3--

Copy and paste that in, and the database version should show up where you saw '2' before.
That worked, I see the version string now. Is there a way to make this faster or more stealthy?

Yes! Use UNION ALL SELECT instead of just UNION SELECT, it can be faster and avoids filtering duplicate rows:

    ' UNION ALL SELECT 1,@@version,3--

Try running that to get the same info, but with better performance.
Nice, that works too. Any other comments I can use to avoid syntax errors?

Definitely. For MySQL, you can use # for line comments as well:

    ' UNION ALL SELECT 1,@@user,3#

Try pasting that in to see the current database user. The # will ignore the rest of the SQL line.
Cool, I see the database user now. Thanks for the help!
Glad it worked! If you need to extract more info, just swap out the payload (like database(), table_name, etc.). Copy these into your testing field as needed!
